entities.name: Baptist Convention of Hong Kong
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Baptist Convention of Hong Kong (Chinese: 香港浸信會聯會) is one of Hong Kong's most significant Protestant denominations, rooted in American Southern Baptist missions that began in Hong Kong in the 1840s-1850s — representing a major stream of Hong Kong Christianity that has contributed significantly to Hong Kong's extensive private educational network, healthcare institutions, and social services over 170+ years of institutional presence.

Hong Kong's Christian community (~11% of the population) has extraordinary institutional significance disproportionate to its size: Christian hospitals, schools, and social service organizations provide a major fraction of Hong Kong's social infrastructure. The Baptist Convention's hospitals (including Baptist Hospital), schools, and social service organizations are among the most important non-government institutions in the territory. Baptist University of Hong Kong (formerly Hong Kong Baptist College, founded 1956) is one of Hong Kong's eight universities.

The Baptist Convention's history in Hong Kong spans the colonial period, the 1949 Communist victory in China that brought a massive wave of mainland Chinese refugees to Hong Kong (swelling Baptist church membership significantly), the economic miracle of Hong Kong's development into a global financial center, and now the complex post-2020 political situation following the National Security Law that has raised questions about Hong Kong civil society's future. The Convention's institutional networks are among Hong Kong's most important civil society infrastructure.
